subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Show that the equation of the tangent to the curve √x + √y = √a at the point (x₁, y₁) is x·x₁⁻¹⁄² + y·y₁⁻¹⁄² = a¹⁄².

mark_split.label: Form the tangent and clear the surds

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how you differentiate the curve, what the slope is at the given point, and which given fact you use in the last line.

steps.label: Differentiate the curve implicitly
steps.margin_note: First mark. Do not make y the subject first. Differentiating √x + √y = √a term by term takes one line, because √a is a constant and its derivative is 0.
lines: Given curve:  √x + √y = √a,  where a is a constant.
Differentiate both sides with respect to x:

recall.must_convey: That implicit differentiation of √x + √y = √a gives dy/dx = −√y/√x.
accept: differentiate both sides with respect to x implicitly
one by two root x plus one by two root y times dy by dx equals zero
dy by dx is minus root y by root x
implicit differentiation chesi dy by dx teesukovali
root a is a constant so its derivative is zero
the derivative of root y needs the chain rule with dy by dx
heard_as: minus root y by root x

steps.why: Squaring the equation to remove the surds produces a cross term 2√(xy) and makes the working longer. Implicit differentiation keeps every term in the form the final answer needs.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the dy/dx factor on the √y term.
Treating √a as a function of x and differentiating it to something other than 0.
Squaring both sides first and then losing a term in the expansion.
steps.memory_tip: Each square root differentiates to 1 over twice itself, and any term in y carries dy/dx behind it.

steps.label: Write the slope at (x₁, y₁)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The point (x₁, y₁) is on the curve, so it satisfies √x₁ + √y₁ = √a. Write that line down here — it is the fact the last step needs.
lines: The point (x₁, y₁) lies on the curve, so
Slope of the tangent at (x₁, y₁):

recall.must_convey: That the slope at (x₁, y₁) is −√y₁/√x₁, and that the point satisfies √x₁ + √y₁ = √a.
accept: substitute x one and y one to get the slope

point curve meeda undi kabatti root x one plus root y one equals root a
write down the on the curve condition before forming the tangent
slope at the given point is minus root y one over root x one
heard_as: root y one by root x one

steps.why: The relation √x₁ + √y₁ = √a is the only place the letter a can enter the final answer, so it has to be written explicitly before the tangent is formed.
common_mistakes: Leaving the slope as −√y/√x with general x and y instead of the point.
Never writing √x₁ + √y₁ = √a, which leaves no way to reach √a at the end.
Writing the slope as −√x₁/√y₁ with the two swapped.
steps.memory_tip: Two facts belong to the point: it satisfies the curve, and it fixes the slope. Write both before touching the tangent.

steps.label: Form the tangent and clear the surds
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Multiply through by √x₁ at once. Working with a fraction of surds through the next two lines is where the algebra usually breaks.
lines: Tangent at (x₁, y₁):  y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)

recall.must_convey: That y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) with m = −√y₁/√x₁ rearranges to √y₁ x + √x₁ y = √y₁ x₁ + √x₁ y₁.
accept: use y minus y one equals m into x minus x one
multiply by root x one to clear the fraction
root y one x plus root x one y equals root y one x one plus root x one y one
point slope form rasi root x one tho multiply cheyyali
bring the x and y terms to the left side
clear the surd in the denominator first
heard_as: m into x minus x one

steps.why: The required answer has x and y on the left and a single constant on the right, so the tangent is rearranged into that shape before anything is simplified.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign when multiplying out −(√y₁/√x₁)(x − x₁).
Multiplying only the left side by √x₁.
Writing the point-slope form as y − y₁ = m(x + x₁).
steps.memory_tip: Point-slope first, denominator cleared second, terms collected third — always in that order.

steps.label: Use √x₁ + √y₁ = √a to finish
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The right side of (ii) factorises as √(x₁y₁)(√x₁ + √y₁). That factor is √a by (i), and dividing by √(x₁y₁) produces exactly the printed form.
lines: By (i), √x₁ + √y₁ = √a, so the right side is √(x₁y₁)·√a.

lines.text: ∴ x·x₁⁻¹⁄² + y·y₁⁻¹⁄² = a¹⁄², which is the required equation of the tangent.

recall.must_convey: That the right side factorises to √(x₁y₁)(√x₁ + √y₁) = √(x₁y₁)·√a, and dividing by √(x₁y₁) gives x/√x₁ + y/√y₁ = √a.

steps.why: A negative half power is the same as one over a square root, so x/√x₁ and x·x₁⁻¹⁄² are the same term written two ways. Saying that line is what connects the working to the printed form.
common_mistakes: Dividing by √x₁y₁ on the left only.
Stopping at √y₁ x + √x₁ y = √(x₁y₁)·√a without dividing, so the printed form is never reached.
steps.memory_tip: A negative power turns the term upside down and a half power is a square root, so x₁⁻¹⁄² is simply 1/√x₁.
